correctness.rationale: The heavy-coordinate argument proves the complete infinite statement. If two codewords both have a coordinate of multiplicity at least three in the same alphabet position, their multiset intersection has size at least three, so their heavy-coordinate sets must be pairwise disjoint. For length at least seven every ternary composition has a heavy coordinate, giving at most three codewords and the three constant words attain the bound. At length six the unique heavy-free composition is \((2,2,2)\); at length five the heavy-free words are the three permutations of \((2,2,1)\), any two of which intersect in four symbols. These facts give the sharp upper bound four at lengths five and six, attained by the displayed witnesses. The package verifier exhaustively confirms the two boundary lengths, and an independent exact set-packing reconstruction also returned maxima four, four, and three at lengths five, six, and seven. The unbounded part rests on the analytic pigeonhole argument, not the finite computations.
residual_risks: The result is specific to alphabet size three and received-multiset size three.
